source_note: Reed 1913 Football for Public and Player, 295 PDF pages; 257 text-bearing, 32 zero-char illustration/diagram plates; printed prose ends p242 then blank/ad pages. Full OCR prose layer readable, zero equations, no retraction notice, no betting chapter. Diagram pages carry OCR noise but all quoted prose is clean and verbatim.

primitives.name: Wind-conditioned tempo invariant: with the wind play fast and kick early to press the advantage; against the wind play slowly, run for time, and conserve strength for the turn
primitives.verbatim_quote: No matter what the plan of generalship used, here are three things that every team should remember: (1) With the wind play fast: against it play slowly.
primitives.latex: Source prints prose coaching doctrine with zero equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. \forall s:\ \mathrm{WithWind}(s)\Rightarrow \mathrm{PlayFast}(s)\land\mathrm{KickEarly}(s),\quad \mathrm{AgainstWind}(s)\Rightarrow \mathrm{PlaySlow}(s)\land\mathrm{Conserve}(s),\quad \mathrm{Conserve}(s)\Rightarrow \mathrm{Fresh}\big(s_{turn}\big)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: s = game state (possession, field position, wind relative to attacking direction) [state]; WithWind/AgainstWind = wind sign relative to the direction of attack [0/1]; PlayFast/PlaySlow = qualitative tempo policy, high vs low play rate and exertion [ordinal, dimensionless]; KickEarly = kick on first or second down rather than waiting [0/1]; Conserve = minimize exertion and use second-string backs [0/1]; Fresh(s_turn) = team condition at the moment the wind turns [ordinal]. No printed numeric formula; the implications formalize '(1) With the wind play fast: against it play slowly.'
primitives.assumptions: Wind is the dominant environmental factor (printed p236 'The wind is the most important factor in football generalship to-day'); the against-wind team runs three downs and kicks low, hard, and out of bounds on the fourth (printed p220); the most powerful backs are kept on the side lines during the desultory time-saving game (printed p220); the wind advantage is temporary and reverses between periods (printed zone chart assumes the wind at the back).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when there is little or no wind, in which case both teams play as if each had a mild wind behind it and the generalship base is symmetric (printed p220); a misplay giving the against-wind team possession within striking distance overrides the slow policy and turns on the full running and passing strength (printed p220); heavy footing or rain degrades the kicking game the fast policy relies on (printed Yale-Princeton 1911 mud example).

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to resource-tempo / energy-budget control under a reversing environmental advantage: when a transient external resource favors you, accelerate expenditure to convert it before it reverses; when it opposes you, minimize expenditure and preserve capacity for the reversal. The printed fast/slow rule is the football instantiation of state-conditioned tempo control with a conservation constraint.
layer2.telemetry: play rate and exertion by wind state; kicking-down distribution with vs against wind; late-game freshness and scoring differential after the wind reverses.

primitives.name: Play-revelation reservation rule: never spend an original or high-class running play in your own territory, where its diagnosis costs future scoring value; exercise it only in opponent territory or when beaten with about a minute left
primitives.verbatim_quote: Never use an original or high-class running play until in opponent's territory. The only exception is when beaten and there is only a minute or so left to play.
primitives.latex: Source prints prose coaching doctrine with zero equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. \mathrm{Reveal}(p)\Rightarrow \mathrm{Diagnosed}(p),\quad \forall p\in\mathrm{HighClass}:\ \mathrm{Use}(p)\Rightarrow x\ge x_{opp},\quad \mathrm{Beaten}\land \tau\le\tau_{min}\Rightarrow \mathrm{Use}(p)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p = a play from the repertoire [categorical]; HighClass = original or high-class running plays [subset]; Reveal(p) = using p where the opponent can scout it [0/1]; Diagnosed(p) = opponent has read and prepared for p [0/1]; x = field position toward the opponent goal [yd]; x_opp = opponent-territory threshold [yd]; tau = time remaining [min]; tau_min = about one minute [printed 'a minute or so']; Use(p) = exercising the play [0/1]. No printed numeric formula; the implications formalize 'Never use an original or high-class running play until in opponent's territory' with its printed exception.
primitives.assumptions: The opponent scouts and diagnoses plays (printed diagnosis chapters; Reginald Brown calls off play after play before the ball is snapped, p284); a play revealed in own territory can be diagnosed before it is needed to score (printed p222 'lest he have them diagnosed when we get into his territory'); the only exception is when beaten with about a minute left to play (printed p228).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when the game is already lost and time is short, so option value vanishes and the best play must be exercised at once (printed exception); fails against an opponent who cannot scout or adapt, where revelation carries no future cost; a play held back too long may never be used if the team never reaches opponent territory.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to option-value / information-asset management: a novel play is a scarce information asset whose value is destroyed by premature revelation because the opponent best-responds once it is diagnosed, so it is reserved for the state where its payoff is highest and exercised early only when the horizon collapses (beaten, one minute left) and option value goes to zero. The printed reservation rule is the football instantiation of exercising an option at expiry rather than burning it early.
layer2.telemetry: first-revelation field position of high-class plays; opponent diagnosis rate after revelation; scoring yield of reserved vs early-revealed plays.

primitives.name: Field-zone action policy: partition the field into kicking-defense, field-goal, and kicking-attack zones and select the kick form by zone, distance punt early, placement from the thirty, quick drop from the twenty
primitives.verbatim_quote: The territory within which it may be considered safe to open fire on the crossbar and the uprights is indicated in the diagram by the term "field goal zone" while the short punting attack may well wait until within that part of the field labeled in the diagram "zone of kicking attack."
primitives.latex: Source prints prose coaching doctrine with zero equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. \pi^{*}(x)=\begin{cases}\mathrm{DistancePunt} & x\in Z_{kd}\\ \mathrm{PlacementFG} & x\in Z_{fg}\\ \mathrm{ShortPlacePunt} & x\in Z_{ka}\end{cases},\quad \mathrm{Placement}(30),\quad \mathrm{DropKick}(20)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x = field position toward the opponent goal [yd]; pi*(x) = zone-conditioned kick-form policy [categorical action]; Z_kd = zone of kicking defense, own territory where the team kicks on first down [region, yd]; Z_fg = field-goal zone, safe to open fire on the crossbar and uprights [region, yd]; Z_ka = zone of kicking attack, short placing punts [region, yd]; Placement(30) = placement field goal from scrimmage at the thirty-yard line [printed yd]; DropKick(20) = quick drop-kick at the twenty-yard line [printed yd]. No printed numeric formula; the piecewise policy formalizes the printed zone diagram (Fig. 8) and its thirty- and twenty-yard prescriptions.
primitives.assumptions: The team is defensively strong with a fine kicker and little running game (printed p204 'planned especially for teams that are defensively strong and have a fine kicker'); the wind is at the back (printed Fig. 8); the placement at thirty leaves an extra man behind the line to recover a fumble (printed p203-204); the drop-kick at twenty allows plenty of room behind the line (printed p204); zone boundaries shift with kicker ability (printed 'might even stop at the center of the field, had the team a kicker like Brickley').
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails for a team with a strong running game, which uses the alternate zone map (Fig. 1) and runs in the attack zone; a weak kicker compresses the field-goal zone and forces earlier distance punts; against the wind the whole scheme is replaced by three slow downs and a low fourth-down kick (printed p220); the placement preference assumes a reliable holder and snap under 1913 conditions.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to state-dependent policy / region-partitioned control: the optimal action is a piecewise function of the state (field position), each region carrying a different action and risk profile, with region boundaries parameterized by capability (kicker strength). The printed zone chart is the football instantiation of a lookup policy over a partitioned state space rather than a single universal action.
layer2.telemetry: kick form selected by zone; field-goal attempt distance and success; fumble-recovery rate on placement vs drop; zone-boundary sensitivity to kicker range.

primitives.name: Tail-risk-bounded placing punt: from the forty near center, put the ball out of bounds just short of the ten rather than drive it closer, eliminating the wind-bounce touchback branch that hands the defense a fresh kick
primitives.verbatim_quote: Once on the forty-yard line and near the center of the field the punter should put the ball out of bounds just short of the ten-yard line. To drive it down closer might be risky, for were the leather to strike just inside and take a bound inward the wind might carry it across the goal line for a touchback, and the touchback is the one thing to be avoided since the defense may bring the ball out and kick.
primitives.latex: Source prints prose coaching doctrine with zero equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. z^{*}=\mathrm{OOB}\ \text{just short of}\ 10\ \mathrm{yd},\quad P(\mathrm{touchback}\mid z^{*})=0,\quad P(\mathrm{touchback}\mid z<10)>0,\quad \mathrm{Touchback}\Rightarrow \mathrm{OppBall}(20)\land\mathrm{OppKick}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: z = punt landing point measured from the opponent goal [yd]; z* = chosen out-of-bounds landing just short of the ten-yard line [printed yd]; OOB = out of bounds [0/1]; P(touchback|z) = probability the wind carries an inward bound across the goal line [0/1, dimensionless]; OppBall(20) = opponent possession brought out to the twenty [printed touchback spot, yd]; OppKick = the defense may bring the ball out and kick [0/1]. No printed numeric formula; the zero-probability claim formalizes 'the touchback is the one thing to be avoided since the defense may bring the ball out and kick' by choosing the out-of-bounds branch.
primitives.assumptions: The wind blows diagonally down the field and can carry an inward bound across the goal line (printed p203); a touchback lets the defense bring the ball out and kick, resetting possession (printed p203); an out-of-bounds kick prevents a run-back and gives the enemy the ball in an awkward position (printed p203); the forty-yard line near the center of the field is the printed trigger for this punt.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when there is no wind to carry the ball, so driving it closer is safe and the out-of-bounds constraint wastes potential territory; near the sideline the printed rule changes to a short straight punt down the field (printed p203); a kicker who cannot place accurately cannot execute the bounded landing and faces the stochastic branch anyway.

layer2.mapping: Derived tail-risk-elimination / bounded-loss placing kernel: choose the landing point that zeroes the probability of the worst possession-reset branch (a touchback giving the opponent a fresh kick at the twenty) even at the cost of a few yards of expected territory, rather than maximizing expected punt distance under a stochastic wind-bounce. The printed 'just short of the ten' is the qualitative seed of a chance-constrained placing rule.
layer2.telemetry: touchback rate on placing punts; out-of-bounds landing accuracy; opponent drive-start field position after the punt; yards sacrificed vs touchback probability eliminated.

primitives.name: Matching-coins deception endgame: once generalship approaches a standard, guess the other coach's expectation of your eleven and choose between doing the expected and the unexpected to maximize deception
primitives.verbatim_quote: In other words the guessing match will have to begin with a guess as to the other coach's opinion and expectation of any particular eleven, and end with a decision as to whether greater deception will be accomplished by doing the expected, or by doing the un- expected. Simply put, it is a case of matching coins all over again.
primitives.latex: Source prints prose coaching doctrine with zero equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. a^{*}=\arg\max_{a\in\{E,U\}} D\big(a,\hat{e}_{opp}\big),\quad \hat{e}_{opp}=f(\mathrm{standard\ generalship}),\quad \mathrm{OppBestResponds}\Rightarrow \text{no pure }a^{*}\Rightarrow \text{mix}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: a = coach's choice {E = do the expected, U = do the unexpected} [categorical]; D(a, e_opp) = deception achieved given the opponent's expectation [ordinal, dimensionless]; e_opp = the other coach's opinion and expectation of this eleven [belief]; f(standard generalship) = expectation formed from the shared standard [mapping]; OppBestResponds = the opponent adapts to any predictable choice [0/1]; mix = randomize over E and U [policy]. No printed numeric formula; the argmax formalizes 'a guess as to the other coach's opinion and expectation ... whether greater deception will be accomplished by doing the expected, or by doing the unexpected' and 'a case of matching coins all over again'.
primitives.assumptions: Generalship has approached a common standard so both coaches share a baseline expectation (printed p267-268); the opponent is a thinking coach who best-responds (printed 'fooling himself were he coaching the opposing eleven'); the variation must not disorganize your own eleven (printed p268 'retain all that is fundamentally sound'); the rule applies only to coaching systems thoroughly up to date (printed p268).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails against an opponent who does not share the standard or cannot diagnose, where doing the fundamentally sound expected play dominates deception; a variation that disorganizes your own team loses more than the deception gains (printed constraint); if one coach is far ahead of the standard the guessing match collapses into executing superior fundamentals.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to matching-pennies / mixed-strategy reasoning: when both players share a standard and each best-responds to the other's predictable choice, no pure strategy is stable, so the coach must form a second-order belief about the opponent's expectation and randomize between the expected and the unexpected. The printed 'matching coins' is the football instantiation of a symmetric guessing game with no pure-strategy equilibrium.
layer2.telemetry: predictability of play choice vs the standard; opponent pre-snap alignment correctness; deception success rate of expected vs unexpected choices; frequency of variation that disorganizes own execution.

primitives.name: Local-information generalship override: the quarterback on the field sees the defense's flaw better than the coaches and may violate the laid-out generalship when his instant observation beats the precommitted plan
primitives.verbatim_quote: Had Hyatt adhered to the generalship laid out for him he would have swung his next play to the right, but in an instant he noticed that the Yale defensive backs were out of position, and instantly changing his generalship he shot another play over to the left and away from the goal posts.
primitives.latex: Source prints prose coaching doctrine with zero equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. \mathrm{Override}\iff I_{field}>I_{plan},\quad \mathrm{Obs}(\mathrm{backs\ out\ of\ position})\Rightarrow \mathrm{Deviate}(\mathrm{plan}),\quad \mathrm{Deviate}\land \mathrm{Sound}(\mathrm{core})\Rightarrow \mathrm{Gain}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I_field = information available to the quarterback at the snap from his field position [ordinal]; I_plan = information encoded in the coaches' precommitted generalship [ordinal]; Override = violate the laid-out plan [0/1]; Obs(backs out of position) = instant observation of a defensive flaw [0/1]; Deviate(plan) = choose a different play than planned [0/1]; Sound(core) = the variation retains what is fundamentally sound [0/1]; Gain = resulting advantage [ordinal]. No printed numeric formula; the biconditional formalizes 'from his position on the field he could see the flaw in Yale's defense far better than they, and thus violated the generalship and gained the victory'.
primitives.assumptions: The coaches' plan is sound as a baseline (printed 'Had Hyatt adhered to the generalship laid out for him he could not have been censured'); the quarterback occupies a field position that reveals the defensive backs' alignment (printed p275); sideline coaching is barred so the on-field man must decide (printed penalty summary p248); the override must not disorganize the eleven (printed p268).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when the quarterback lacks the judgment to read the flaw, so the override is noise rather than information; a deviation that abandons the fundamentally sound core disorganizes the team (printed constraint); when the plan already encodes the same information the override adds nothing and risks execution error.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to decentralized decision / local-information advantage (mission command): a precommitted plan encodes the commander's prior information, but the agent on the spot holds fresher local information at the moment of action, so authority devolves to the local agent when his observation dominates the plan, provided the deviation preserves the intent. The printed Hyatt override is the football instantiation of letting local information beat a stale prior.
layer2.telemetry: override frequency and success rate; information lag between coach plan and field observation; scoring yield of overridden vs adhered plays; disorganization rate after deviation.

reasoning_traces.think: Begin with Reed's treatment of the wind as a strategic resource rather than as weather. The printed invariant is blunt: with the wind play fast, against it play slowly. This is a state-conditioned tempo policy, and its logic is an energy budget under a reversing advantage. When the wind is at your back every exchange of kicks favors you, so you accelerate the game, kick on first down, and press the advantage before the periods turn; when the wind opposes you there is nothing to do but run three downs, kick low and hard and out of bounds on the fourth, and above all run the plays slowly, playing for time and making as little exertion as possible so as to be fresh when your turn comes with the wind. The most powerful backs are deliberately kept on the side lines during this desultory time-saving game, which is a conservation constraint written into the policy. The zone chart is the spatial counterpart of the same idea: the field is partitioned into a zone of kicking defense, a field-goal zone, and a zone of kicking attack, and the optimal kick form is a piecewise function of position, distance punt early, placement from the thirty, quick drop from the twenty. These printed yard lines are policy thresholds, not measurements of a physical law. The touchback-avoidance rule is the risk constraint that bounds the placing punt: from the forty near center the punter puts the ball out of bounds just short of the ten, because driving it closer risks an inward bound the wind carries across the goal line for a touchback, and the touchback is the one thing to be avoided since the defense may bring the ball out and kick. Choosing the out-of-bounds branch zeroes the probability of that worst possession-reset branch at the cost of a few yards of territory. What is sovereign across all three primitives is that possession value is position-dependent and the kicking game is a territorial instrument whose tail risk must be bounded at the goal line. The isomorphisms are exact in structure: tempo control under a reversing resource, a lookup policy over a partitioned state space, and a chance-constrained placing rule. The telemetry that would falsify them is play rate by wind state, kick form by zone, and touchback rate, not raw punting distance.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This zone-and-wind generalship is a direct product of the 1912 rule changes, which abolished the onside kick, restricted the forward pass, and freed the punter from the old five-yard-back requirement. Reed writes just after Princeton defeated both Harvard and Yale without the semblance of a running attack, and after Felton's deadly placing punts of 1912, so the kicking game had become the dominant strategic instrument. The genealogy runs from the old run-until-stopped-then-kick habit to a position-first policy, caused by the new rules' geometry making territory, not possession, the objective.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Reed models the opponent as an anticipator with down-based priors: the against-wind team is expected to punt on the fourth down, so the with-wind team's first-down kick is surprising precisely because it violates that prior. The touchback rule models both the referee's impetus rule and the opponent's right to bring the ball out and kick, so the coach reasons about what the opponent will do with the resulting possession. The conservation policy models his own players' fatigue, keeping the best backs fresh for the moment the wind turns.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The position-value layer vetoes any primitive that treats the zone thresholds as a physical law or a modern analytics equation; the thirty and twenty are 1913 policy parameters under 1913 rules, including the touchback spot and placement-versus-drop scoring. It vetoes importing modern punt analytics as if printed, since the coffin-corner descendant is not the wind-bounce-specific rule Reed states. It also vetoes reading play fast or slow as a measured tempo statistic; it is a qualitative exertion-and-clock policy, and the veto keeps the formalization labeled rather than fabricated.

reasoning_traces.think: Turn to Reed's economics of information, where a play is a scarce asset rather than a mere action. The reservation rule is explicit: never use an original or high-class running play until in opponent's territory, lest the opponent have it diagnosed before you get into his territory. This is an option-value rule. Revealing a novel play in your own territory lets the opponent read and prepare for it, destroying its future scoring value for the sake of a small present gain, so the play is reserved for the state where its payoff is highest. The single printed exception, when beaten and there is only a minute or so left to play, is the standard option-expiry logic: when the horizon collapses, option value vanishes and you exercise the asset immediately. The forward pass is the same logic applied to a threat rather than a play. Reed insists the pass is quite as valuable as a threat as an actual play, because the menace alone forces an opening out of the defense, and the defense cannot possibly cover five men, four will make serious trouble. So the threat spreads the defense even when the pass is not forthcoming, and the wise coach mixes the threat and the actual play. The endgame of this information war is Reed's matching-coins passage: once generalship approaches a standard, the strategist must guess the other coach's opinion and expectation of his eleven and decide whether greater deception is accomplished by doing the expected or by doing the unexpected, simply a case of matching coins all over again. This is a symmetric guessing game with no pure-strategy solution, because each coach best-responds to the other's predictable choice. The physical instantiation is the jump shift against the sliding defense: the attack tries to catch the defense in lateral motion at the snap, while the defense can slide faster than the attack can jump because it is not obliged to have a man come over the ball. The sovereign lesson is that information, like territory, is a resource to be reserved, threatened, and randomized, and that the value of a play lies partly in its unrevealed potential.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The reservation rule descends from the era's scouting and diagnosis culture, which Reed documents in the Minot punt-drift scouting and in Reginald Brown calling off play after play before the ball is snapped. The matching-coins passage is Reed's 1913 forecast of what happens when coaching knowledge diffuses and team types converge toward a standard, so that novelty must be built on fundamental principle rather than on secrecy. The forward-pass threat doctrine inherits the Rules Committee's stated intent to spread the defense rather than to reward the pass itself.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Reed reasons explicitly at second order: the coach must form a guess as to the other coach's opinion and expectation, that is, model the opponent's model of his own team. The pass threat works because the defense must reckon with the menace even when no pass comes, so the coach exploits the opponent's compelled attention. The reservation rule models the opponent as a diagnoser who will best-respond to any revealed play, which is why revelation is treated as a cost rather than a free action.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The information layer vetoes labeling any of this a printed game-theory equation: Reed prints no payoff matrix and no equilibrium frequency, so the matching-pennies reading is a labeled isomorphism, not a source formula. It vetoes importing modern mixed-strategy frequencies as if measured. It also vetoes treating the five-receiver coverage claim as a modern route-concept statistic; it is a 1913 eligibility-count argument, four backs and two ends minus the passer, and the veto preserves that historical substrate rather than normalizing it.

reasoning_traces.think: Finally examine Reed's doctrine of delegated generalship, which disciplines how the preceding policies are actually executed. The generalship chart is a precommitted plan, but Reed insists the plan must be violable by the man on the field. The worked example is Hyatt's 1911 touchdown against Yale on a morass: the generalship laid out for him called for swinging the next play to the right to bring the ball out for a field goal, but in an instant Hyatt noticed that the Yale defensive backs were out of position and, instantly changing his generalship, shot another play over to the left and away from the goal posts, scoring the only touchdown of the day. Reed's verdict is the principle itself: from his position on the field Hyatt could see the flaw in Yale's defense far better than the coaches, and thus violated the generalship and gained the victory. This is a local-information override. The plan encodes the coaches' prior information; the quarterback holds fresher, local information at the snap; when the two conflict, the local observation wins. The same structure appears in Poe asking for his chance, where the player rather than the coach detects the psychological moment, and in Field's desperate tackle that saved Yale. The invariant is that a plan is a prior, not a command: its value is the baseline it provides, and the value of the override is the information gain over that baseline. Reed bounds the override with a constraint drawn from his future-strategy chapter: the variation must retain all that is fundamentally sound and must not disorganize his own eleven. So the override is licensed only by superior local information, not by whim. The sovereign lesson is that centralized planning and decentralized execution are complementary, and that the right to deviate belongs to the agent whose observation is freshest, provided the deviation preserves the intent.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The delegation doctrine grows from the era's ban on sideline coaching, which Reed lists in the penalty summary as a five-yard penalty, so the rules themselves force decision authority onto the on-field captain. Reed's sustained warfare analogy supplies the vocabulary of the general on the field who must act on what he sees rather than on a stale plan. The genealogy runs from the coach-as-dictator model to a mission-command model, caused by the rule that removed the coach from the field during play.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Reed models the coach as needing to trust his quarterback's judgment, and the quarterback as needing to model the coaches' intent well enough to deviate productively rather than randomly. The override is a theory-of-mind act in both directions: the coach anticipates that the field man will see more, and the field man anticipates what the coach was trying to achieve so his deviation serves the intent. The opponent's defensive alignment is the third mind read, the flaw Hyatt detects in an instant.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The delegation layer vetoes reading Hyatt's override as a refutation of planning: Reed explicitly says adherence to the laid-out generalship would not have been censured, so the plan is sound and the violation is licensed only by superior local information. It vetoes importing a modern analytics-versus-coach framing, since the printed claim is about information locality, not about data. It also vetoes any override that abandons the fundamentally sound core, because the printed constraint rejects variation that disorganizes the eleven.

universal_lens: Across domains Reed is a study of decision under adversarial uncertainty: partition the state space into zones with different optimal actions, condition tempo on a reversing environmental resource, reserve scarce information assets until their payoff is highest, bound the tail risk of the worst possession-reset branch, randomize between the expected and the unexpected when both sides share a standard, and let fresher local observation override a stale precommitted plan. These are universal principles of state-dependent policy, option value, chance-constrained risk, mixed strategy, and decentralized authority, expressed in 1913 football prose with zero equations.
gsi_mapping: For the General Sovereignty Institute Reed supplies sovereign decision kernels: a wind-conditioned tempo invariant with a conservation constraint, a play-revelation option-value rule, a region-partitioned kick-form policy, a tail-risk-elimination placing kernel, a matching-coins mixed-strategy endgame, and a local-information generalship override. Each is extracted as a labeled predicate-logic formalization of printed prose, never a fabricated equation, preserving the 1913 yard-line thresholds and rule substrate verbatim and pairing every structural principle with the regime where it fails, which is the institute's standard for scientific rather than dogmatic doctrine.
gse_mapping: For the Game Sovereignty Engine these primitives map to football decision modules: wind-aware tempo and kick scheduling, zone-conditioned kick-form selection, reservation of high-class plays until opponent territory, chance-constrained placing punts that avoid the touchback branch, deception mixing against a shared standard, and a quarterback override gated by local-information advantage. The engine can encode play rate by wind state, kick form by zone, first-revelation field position, touchback rate, predictability versus the standard, and override success as falsifiable telemetry, while respecting the 1913 rules and the constraint that variation must not disorganize the eleven, so the modules stay grounded in the printed source rather than in modern normalized assumptions.
